morphology.motility: Motile via periplasmic flagella, corkscrew motion
morphology.notes: Often reclassified taxonomically to genus Borreliella; commonly still referred to clinically as Borrelia burgdorferi

habitat.naturalHabitat: Maintained in a natural cycle between Ixodes ticks and small mammal/bird reservoir hosts (e.g. white-footed mice)
habitat.hostAssociation: Zoonotic — humans are incidental, dead-end hosts
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Endemic to wooded/grassy areas in parts of North America, Europe, and Asia where Ixodes ticks are established
habitat.reservoir: Small mammals (especially white-footed mice), Ixodes ticks

microscopy.stain: Not routinely visualized by Gram stain (poorly staining, low organism burden in clinical specimens)
microscopy.appearance: Loosely coiled spirochete on specialized silver stains/dark-field microscopy

culture.growthCharacteristics: Fastidious, very slow growing — culture is rarely used clinically
culture.colonyMorphology: Not applicable — grows in liquid medium, not as discrete colonies

biochemicalTests.test: Two-tiered serology (EIA screen, Western blot confirmation)

identificationClues: Diagnosis is primarily clinical (erythema migrans rash) plus two-tiered serologic testing, not culture
Erythema migrans — an expanding "bull's-eye" rash at the tick-bite site is the classic early clinical sign
History of tick exposure in an endemic wooded/grassy area
Culture on BSK medium exists but is rarely used clinically due to slow, fastidious growth

diseases: Lyme disease — early localized (erythema migrans), early disseminated (multiple erythema migrans, carditis, facial palsy), and late disease (Lyme arthritis, neuroborreliosis)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Bite of an infected Ixodes tick (e.g. Ixodes scapularis, the blacklegged/deer tick); typically requires prolonged tick attachment (about 36-48 hours) for transmission
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: The most common vector-borne illness in North America and parts of Europe, concentrated in regions with established Ixodes tick populations
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Two-tiered serologic testing (screening EIA followed by confirmatory Western blot/second EIA) is the standard diagnostic approach; antibodies may not be detectable in the earliest days of infection

examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Transmitted by Ixodes ticks and requires prolonged tick attachment for transmission, unlike many other vector-borne infections
